$comment: What each slice template family already does, and what it leaves to the developer. scripts/render-slice.py reads this file and reports, for the families it rendered, behaviours[] {id, status, summary, where} and stubTests[] {path, covers[]} in its --json output; the sdd plugin reads that report so its test author writes failing tests only for the placeholder behaviours, and deletes exactly the stub tests listed (so every file under a family's test/ directory must appear in its stubTests). It sits beside the java/ and kotlin/ directories so it is never rendered as a template. Keys are <language>/<family directory>; `where` is a template path relative to that family directory, path placeholders unsubstituted, with an optional #member; a behaviour whose file was not rendered (the __Aggregate__State* pair without --with-state) is dropped by the renderer. Ids are a public contract: never rename or reuse one, and give the same behaviour the same id in every language and lane. The one hard rule is honesty: `implemented` means the rendered skeleton, once it compiles, really does it, so a reasonable test of it passes untouched; anything left as a TODO, a throw, an empty body or a placeholder constant is `placeholder`. When a template changes, change its entries here in the same commit; tests/scripts/test_behaviours_catalog.py checks the structure, not the honesty.

An event whose order is not newer than the row's version is skipped, so a redelivered event changes nothing.
A subscription reset deletes every row, so the replay that follows rebuilds the read model from the events.
A GET on the view's path returns every row of the read model.
